_comment: Golden fixtures for the Polaris polish layer. Each entry documents a dictation pattern, its expected polished output, and the expected intent classification. Run with: GROQ_API_KEY=... cargo test --test polish_golden -- --ignored --nocapture. See the header of tests/polish_golden.rs for what expected_intent is worth and what intent_advisory means: intent has no consumer in the app, so an intent-only mismatch is reported and never fails the run, and a fixture whose expected_intent contradicts POLISH_SYSTEM_PROMPT own form_field length rule MUST carry an intent_advisory saying which two rules collide. tests/polish_golden.rs::fixture_intents_agree_with_the_prompt enforces that offline, with no API calls.

fixtures.raw: mets-moi un rendez-vous pour demain, après-demain
fixtures.intent_advisory: 6 words, no terminal punctuation, so the form_field rule applies; it is also an imperative, so the raw_prompt rule applies. POLISH_SYSTEM_PROMPT states no precedence between them. Asserted as an observation only.
fixtures.notes: The user's original bug report. Lexical self-correction, same semantic class (time), no coordinating conjunction → keep last item. KNOWN FAILING against openai/gpt-oss-120b, deterministically: 7/7 across every rule-5 wording tried on 2026-09-06. It is neither the word pair nor the sentence frame — 'on se voit demain, après-demain', 'je pars demain, après-demain' and 'mets-moi un rendez-vous pour lundi, lundi prochain' all resolve correctly. Only a scheduling imperative plus two bare dates resists, because the model reads the dates as two slots offered to whoever books it. The only wording that fixed it quoted this sentence's own carrier phrase in the prompt and was rejected as teaching to the test; see the rule-5 section of POLISH_SYSTEM_PROMPT's docs in transcription/polish.rs. Left asserting the correct product behaviour on purpose — the 90% threshold absorbs one miss, and weakening this fixture would delete the only record that the defect is real.

fixtures.notes: Rule 5 shape (b): two same-class items, no repair marker, no conjunction. Measured 2026-09-06 — the pre-rewrite prompt kept both; the rewrite drops the superseded one. No expected_intent: the label is unstable here (form_field/natural_text) and has no consumer.

fixtures.notes: Rule 5 shape (b), derivational: the second item contains the first. A shared stem is what a spoken correction sounds like, and the pre-rewrite prompt kept both. Structurally identical to fr_self_correction_lexical_immediate, and this one passes — which is the evidence that the rule is sound and that fixture is a single-sentence model limitation.
